template_name: Surface Material Properties and Haptic Affective Response

mechanism_chain.process: Occupant's hand, foot, or body contacts an architectural surface. Surface material properties — roughness (Ra), thermal conductivity (λ), compliance (Young's modulus E), texture grain orientation — are transduced by mechanoreceptors (Meissner, Pacinian, Merkel, Ruffini) and CT afferents.
mechanism_chain.substrate: Peripheral somatosensory transduction: glabrous and hairy skin receptors

mechanism_chain.process: Material property encoding is dual-process: Aβ mechanoreceptors encode discriminative properties (roughness magnitude, texture spatial frequency, hardness) in SI cortex; CT afferents encode affective valence (pleasant/unpleasant) in posterior insular cortex.
mechanism_chain.substrate: SI cortex (discriminative) + posterior insula (affective) — parallel processing streams

mechanism_chain.process: Material-specific hedonic profiles: wood (warm, moderate roughness, moderate compliance = strongly pleasant); natural stone (cool, smooth to moderate roughness, rigid = neutral to mildly pleasant); metal (cold, very smooth, rigid = mildly aversive); concrete (cold, rough, rigid = moderately aversive); fabric (warm, soft, compliant = strongly pleasant).

thermal_modulation.value: heated metal/stone ≈ +0.25 hedonic score; cooled wood ≈ -0.15 hedonic score
thermal_modulation.interpretation: Surface temperature modulates hedonic response independently of material identity. Heated stone or metal handrails approach wood hedonic levels. Cooling natural materials reduces their haptic pleasantness.

age_group.effect: Reduced tactile sensitivity (higher detection thresholds) may attenuate fine texture discrimination but hedonic valuation pathway is preserved. Thermal sensitivity is maintained; thermal conductivity effects are robust in aging.

IC2_AX4_interaction.IC2_body_budget: Haptic affect from material contact contributes to body budget through the parasympathetic pathway: pleasant touch → insular cortex → parasympathetic activation → body budget credit. Unpleasant touch (cold metal, rough concrete) produces sympathetic activation → body budget debit.
IC2_AX4_interaction.AX4_perceived_control: Choice of contact surface is a control variable. When occupants can choose which surfaces to touch (selecting the wood railing over the metal one), perceived control amplifies the hedonic benefit. When contact is forced (only cold metal surfaces available), the lack of haptic choice compounds the negative affect.

name: Surface Material Properties and Haptic Affective Response

surface_temperature_management.interpretation: Active thermal management of surfaces (heated stone seats, heated metal railings) shifts hedonic scores toward positive range. Passive thermal mass (cold stone in winter) shifts toward negative.

texture_grain_alignment.interpretation: Wood grain aligned with hand-stroke direction (e.g., horizontal on a railing gripped in a slide) produces more pleasant haptic experience than cross-grain contact.
